items.q: Quandō tempestās tam subitō cessāvit?
items.en: When did the storm cease so suddenly?
items.hint: a postquam clause with the perfect indicative

items.q: Utrum corpus an animus Mēdī turbātus est?
items.en: Is it Medus' body or his mind that is troubled?
items.hint: utrum … an offers two subjects; tap the one that is turbātus

items.q: Quis est Chrīstus, ut Lydia dīcit?
items.en: Who is Christ, according to Lydia?
answers: Deī fīlius quī homō factus est
fīlius Deī quī homō factus est
choices: Deī fīlius quī homō factus est
items.hint: a nominative predicate with a relative clause (factus est = 'was made')

items.q: In quō oppidō Chrīstus nātus est?
items.en: In what town was Christ born?
items.hint: in + ablative; the town's name does not decline

items.q: Quid Iēsūs in Iūdaeā verbīs efficiēbat?
items.en: What did Jesus bring about in Judea by his words?
answers: efficiēbat ut mortuī surgerent et ambulārent
ut caecī vidērent, surdī audīrent, mūtī loquerentur
items.hint: efficiēbat ut + the imperfect subjunctive (past main verb → imperfect subjunctive)

items.q: Unde hominēs aegrī ad Iēsum conveniēbant?
items.en: From where did the sick come to Jesus?
items.hint: ex + ablative for place from which

items.q: Ā quō libellus Lydiae scrīptus est?
items.en: By whom was Lydia's little book written?
items.hint: the ablative of agent after ā (ā quōdam Iūdaeō, nōmine Matthaeō)

items.q: Quid Mēdus Lydiam rogat?
items.en: What does Medus ask Lydia to do?
items.hint: an indirect command: rogat ut + present subjunctive (sibi = to him)

items.q: Quid Iāīrus Iēsum rogāvit?
items.en: What did Jairus ask Jesus to do?
items.hint: rogāvit ut + imperfect subjunctive (the main verb is past)

items.q: Num Iuppiter hominem mortālem ab Īnferīs suscitāre potest?
items.en: Jupiter can't raise a mortal man from the Underworld, can he?
answers: Nē Iuppiter quidem tantam potestātem habet
Minimē, nē Iuppiter quidem tantam potestātem habet
items.hint: num expects 'no'; nē … quidem = 'not even'

items.q: Quot diī mundum ūniversum inter sē dīvīsērunt?
items.en: How many gods divided the whole world among themselves?
items.hint: a numeral in the nominative; the ita … ut clause that follows is a result clause

items.q: Quandō Iēsūs ad discipulōs super mare ambulāns vēnit?
items.en: When did Jesus come to the disciples walking on the sea?
items.hint: an ablative of time when with an ordinal number

items.q: Cūr discipulī prae timōre clāmāvērunt?
items.en: Why did the disciples cry out in fear?
answers: quod Iēsum super mare ambulantem vīdērunt
quia eum super mare ambulantem vīdērunt
items.hint: they saw him walking (a present participle in the accusative) and took him for a ghost

items.q: Cūr Petrus super aquam ambulābat?
items.en: Why was Peter walking on the water?
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + imperfect subjunctive after a past main verb

items.q: Quandō ventus cessāvit?
items.en: When did the wind stop?
items.hint: an ablative absolute with a present participle (ascendentibus eīs = as they were climbing in)

items.q: Quid accidit cum tempestās magna in marī facta est?
items.en: What happened when a great storm arose at sea?
items.hint: a result clause: ita ut + imperfect subjunctive (operīrētur)

items.q: Quid factum est postquam Iēsūs ventīs et marī imperāvit?
items.en: What happened after Jesus commanded the winds and the sea?
items.hint: the nominative subject of facta est; imperāre takes the dative (ventīs et marī)

items.q: Cui mare et ventī oboediunt, ut gubernātor dīcit?
items.en: Whom do the sea and the winds obey, according to the helmsman?
items.hint: oboedīre takes the dative; nēminī … nisi = 'no one except'

items.q: Quid Neptūnus cūrāvit, ut gubernātor cēnset?
items.en: What did Neptune see to, in the helmsman's view?
answers: ut ē tempestāte servārentur nēve mergerentur
ut nōs ē tempestāte servārēmur nēve mergerēmur
items.hint: cūrāvit ut … nēve + imperfect subjunctive (past main verb)

items.q: Quālia perīcula nautīs impendent?
items.en: What kinds of danger threaten sailors?
items.hint: three nominative subjects introduced by ut ('such as'), each with a relative clause; the last has a purpose clause (ut … rapiant)

items.q: Quid gubernātor cūrābit?
items.en: What will the helmsman see to?
answers: ut omnia perīcula vītent ac salvī in Graeciam eant
ut omnia perīcula vītēmus ac salvī in Graeciam eāmus
items.hint: cūrābō ut + present subjunctive (a future main verb keeps the present subjunctive)

items.q: Intrā quot diēs nāvis in Graeciam perveniet, ut gubernātor spērat?
items.en: Within how many days will the ship reach Greece, as the helmsman hopes?
items.hint: intrā + accusative ('within six days, or rather eight')

items.q: Utrum gubernātor Rōmae an in Graeciā vīvere māvult?
items.en: Does the helmsman prefer to live at Rome or in Greece?
answers: Rōmae vīvere māvult quam in Graeciā
items.hint: utrum … an; Rōmae is the locative ('at Rome'); mālō = prefer

items.q: Quid cīvēs Rōmānī mālunt quam servīre?
items.en: What do Roman citizens prefer to being slaves?
items.hint: a deponent infinitive after mālō … quam

items.q: Cūr Mēdus herī ē vīllā fūgit?
items.en: Why did Medus flee from the villa yesterday?
answers: ut verbera vītāret atque ut amīcam suam vidēret
ut verbera vītāret et amīcam suam vidēret ac semper cum eā esset
ut verbera vītāret atque amīcam vidēret
ut amīcam suam vidēret ac semper cum eā esset
items.hint: purpose clauses: ut + imperfect subjunctive (vītāret, vidēret, esset)

items.q: Quōmodo Mēdus Lydiae persuāsit ut sēcum ex Italiā proficīscerētur?
items.en: How did Medus persuade Lydia to set out with him from Italy?
items.hint: an ablative of means; persuādeō takes the dative and ut + subjunctive

items.q: Ubi Mēdus et Lydia nāvem cōnscendērunt?
items.en: Where did Medus and Lydia board the ship?
items.hint: the locative of a town name ('at Ostia'); ut nāvigārēmus is a purpose clause

items.q: Servitne Lydia dominō Rōmānō?
items.en: Does Lydia serve a Roman master?
answers: Nēminī servit nisi dominō quī est in caelīs
Nēminī servit nisi dominō nostrō quī est in caelīs
Lydia nēminī servit nisi dominō quī est in caelīs
items.hint: a yes/no question with -ne; servīre takes the dative (nēminī … nisi dominō)

items.q: Quot dominīs nēmō servīre potest?
items.en: How many masters can no one serve?
items.hint: a numeral in the dative plural, because servīre takes the dative

items.q: Quid Mēdus Lydiae prope centum sēstertiīs ēmit?
items.en: What did Medus buy for Lydia for nearly a hundred sesterces?
items.hint: the accusative object of ēmit; sēstertiīs is an ablative of price

items.q: Quid Mēdus rubēns nescit?
items.en: What does the blushing Medus not know?
items.hint: an indirect question: quid + present subjunctive after nescit

items.q: Quem Mēdus celeriter accēdere videt?
items.en: Whom does Medus see approaching quickly?
items.hint: accusative + infinitive after videt (mercātōrem accēdere)

items.q: Quid Nausicaa ancillīs imperābat?
items.en: What was Nausicaa ordering the maids to do?
answers: imperābat ut ad sē pilam mitterent
items.hint: imperābat ut + imperfect subjunctive (past main verb); sē refers back to Nausicaa

items.q: Cūr pila numquam ad terram cadēbat?
items.en: Why did the ball never fall to the ground?
answers: quia puellae tam cupidae erant eam capiendī ut cadere nōn sinerent
quia puellae tam cupidae erant eam capiendī
quod puellae tam cupidae erant eam capiendī
quia puellae cupidae erant eam capiendī
quia puellae eam cadere nōn sinēbant
items.hint: a quia clause containing a result clause (tam … ut + imperfect subjunctive) and a genitive gerund with an object (eam capiendī)

items.q: Cūr Ulixēs rāmum ex arbore frēgit?
items.en: Why did Ulysses break a branch from a tree?
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + imperfect subjunctive

items.q: Quae sōla ex puellīs mānsit?
items.en: Which girl alone stayed?
items.hint: the nominative subject with a genitive attached (Alcinoī fīlia); metū dēpositō is an ablative absolute
